content.title: Major retailer hit with class-action lawsuit over automatic membership renewals
content.text: BusinessBAYONNE, NJ - MARCH 26: People enter and exit a Costco Wholesale store on March 26, 2023, in Bayonne, New Jersey. (Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images)(Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images)By Kelly Corbett | kcorbett@syracuse.comCostco is in some hot water after a California man filed a class-action lawsuit arguing that the warehouse retailer is a little too quiet when it comes to auto-renewing memberships.According to Scripps News, the plaintiff, Russel George, claims Costco broke state rules that require businesses to give customers a heads-up between 15 and 45 days before charging them for another year. George says he was notified before the 45-day window, which was untimely. He and his legal team argued that he doesn’t use his membership enough to justify the cost, and if he’d actually received a reminder about the auto-renewal during the appropriate time frame, he would have pulled the plug before the charge hit his account.Additionally, his lawsuit also takes aim at how hard it is to actually cancel the membership. Currently, if you want out, you have to call a toll-free number or show up at a warehouse in person. However, California law mandates that businesses must allow consumers to cancel using the same method they used to sign up. Therefore, if signed up online, you should be able to cancel online. The state requires a “straightforward” exit strategy, and George’s legal team argues that Costco’s current hurdles don’t quite make the cut.The legal action follows recent federal regulatory developments in the subscription industry. The Federal Trade Commission attempted to establish nationwide “click-to-cancel” rules in 2024 that would have required businesses to make canceling as easy as enrolling. A federal appeals court struck down that regulation in July 2025, determining the agency did not follow proper procedures.A preliminary hearing in George’s case is scheduled for June. Costco currently offers a $65 annual membership and a $130 executive membership.Kelly Corbett is a Trending News Reporter for syracuse.com | The Post-Standard.
